# Appeal of Denial — Hip Arthroscopy (CPT 29914)

**Member:** Casey Hayes
**Member ID:** W225149976
**Payer/Plan:** Cigna (Commercial/ACA), Illinois
**Denial date:** 2026-08-11
**Reference number:** POC-8E43F25837-44913
**Governing policy:** Cigna CMM-314 Hip Surgery - Arthroscopic and Open Procedures V1.0.2026 (effective 2026-08-04) — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-314%20Hip%20Surg%20Arthro%20%26%20Open%20Proc_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

Dear Cigna Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my hip arthroscopy (CPT 29914), noted in the letter above with reference number POC-8E43F25837-44913. My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking Cigna to reconsider this decision.

The denial states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I want to walk through the specific criteria in Cigna's own policy and show where the records in my file already address them, so the reviewer can see what documentation supports this request.

## The Plan's Criteria and My Records

Cigna's policy states:

> "femoroacetabular impingement (FAI) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

My imaging and clinical records show findings consistent with this diagnosis. My MRI arthrogram of the hip, performed 2026-06-08, documented an anterosuperior labral tear with cam-type femoroacetabular impingement, an alpha angle of 68 degrees, preserved joint space, and Tonnis grade 0.

The policy also states:

> "◦ positive anterior impingement sign (i.e., groin-dominant hip pain with forced hip flexion, adduction, and internal rotation) ◦ limited passive hip internal rotation • Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration AND which must include the following (unless contraindicated):"

My exam findings document positive provocative testing on the affected hip and range of motion limited by pain. My symptoms are groin-dominant: I have sharp anterior groin pain with sitting and pivoting, and I am unable to run or squat. [Reviewer note: if the plan requires the exam finding to be specifically labeled "anterior impingement sign," my surgeon's office can confirm how this finding was documented in the chart.]

On the non-surgical management requirement, my records show more than three months of provider-directed treatment:

- NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief
- Supervised physical therapy focused on core and hip stabilization with activity modification, 18 visits over 8 weeks (2026-05-26 to 2026-07-21), documented in the physical therapy discharge note
- A corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-23, which gave only 3 weeks of partial relief

Taken together, these treatments span well beyond three months and reflect an inadequate response to non-surgical care.

The policy excerpts provided to me also list non-indications and non-medically-necessary uses for hip arthroscopy, synovectomy, and certain experimental procedures. My request is for hip arthroscopy to address a labral tear with cam-type FAI, which is not one of the excluded indications described above. If Cigna's review found that my documentation matched one of these non-indication categories, I am asking for clarification on which specific finding was thought to apply, since my chart does not reflect any of the excluded conditions listed.

## What I Am Asking

I am requesting that Cigna reconsider this denial in light of the clinical documentation described above, which I understand is already part of my prior authorization file. If any specific piece of documentation is still considered missing or unclear, I would appreciate a specific description of what is needed so my surgeon's office can supply it promptly.

## Deadline and Where I Am Sending This

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-07. I am submitting this through my.cigna.com and/or by calling 1-800-244-6224, and I am also sending it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, since that address is specific to my plan.

Thank you for reviewing this appeal.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Casey Hayes
Member ID: W225149976
Date: [date of signing]
Contact phone: [phone number]
Contact email: [email address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
